section_summary: This section documents the development and execution of U.S. and Allied occupation policy concerning intellectual property and copyright protection in occupied Japan between 1946 and 1948. It focuses on debates within the State Department and SANACC regarding the status and potential abrogation of the 1905 U.S.-Japan Copyright Convention, the treatment of unauthorized translations, and interim copyright protection for Allied nationals. It also records the establishment of SCAP's commercial licensing program and competitive bidding system, administered by the Civil Information and Education Section and the Japan Publishers Association, which awarded translation rights for American and British books to Japanese publishers.

subfiles.about: Schuler requests the Legal Adviser's opinion on copyright questions raised by SCAP regarding the 1906 copyright convention and protection in Japan.

subfiles.summary: Requests Legal Adviser's opinion on questions raised by SCAP regarding the 1906 copyright convention and copyright protection in Japan.
subfiles.title: Copyright Problems in Japan

subfiles.from: William W. Bishop, Legal Adviser's Office

subfiles.about: Records a discussion among State Department and Army officials regarding State's objections to the proposed abrogation of the 1905 convention under SANACC 388.

subfiles.summary: Recommends referring SANACC 388 to the Subcommittee for the Far East for urgent study and report due to complex legal problems.
subfiles.title: SANACC 388, Policy for Treatment of U.S. Copyrighted Literary Works in Japan

subfiles.about: Saltzman recommends referring SANACC 388 to SFE for urgent consideration due to the complexity of the problem and lack of detailed information.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, State Member, SANACC
subfiles.summary: Recommends referring SANACC 388 to SFE for study as a matter of urgency rather than direct SANACC consideration.
subfiles.title: SANACC 388, Policy for Treatment of U.S. Copyrighted Literary Works in Japan

subfiles.about: Requests a meeting between State Department and SANACC representatives to discuss Japanese copyright relations, peace treaty clauses, and possible treaty abrogation.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, State Member, SANACC
subfiles.summary: Requests a meeting between State Department and SANACC representatives to consider Japanese copyright relations, treaty clauses, and possible treaty abrogation.
subfiles.title: Copyright Relations with Japan

subfiles.about: Furman analyzes legal, philosophical, and practical issues surrounding the Far Eastern Commission copyright paper, explaining copyright as a statutory monopoly and supporting the PCC compromise.
subfiles.from: John P. Furman, Division of International Resources
subfiles.summary: Furman explains his support for the Policy Committee on Copyright compromise draft regarding the Far Eastern Commission paper on Japanese copyrights. He analyzes copyright as a limited statutory monopoly rather than an inherent natural property right, examining prewar 1905 treaty terms and SCAP's broad occupation powers. He concludes that balancing occupation reorientation needs with fair compensation for translation rights provides the most practical solution.
subfiles.title: FEC Copyright Paper
subfiles.to: Marshall Green, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs

subfiles.about: Transmits an approved copy of SANACC 388/1, noting that its conclusions were sent via the Joint Chiefs of Staff to CINCFE as U.S. policy guidance.

subfiles.summary: Transmits approved copy of SANACC 388/1 regarding copyrighted literary works in Japan, forwarded to CINCFE as U.S. policy guidance.
subfiles.title: SANACC 388/1 (SANA-6060)

subfiles.about: Sebald reports on SCAP's program for competitive bidding on foreign translation rights, transmitting press releases, lists of awarded titles, and sample licenses.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits press releases and sample licenses detailing SCAP's competitive bidding program for Japanese publishers acquiring foreign book translation rights.
subfiles.title: Japanese Publishers' Acquisition of Rights to Translate and Publish Foreign Books (Despatch No. 432)

subfiles.about: CIE announces that an initial list of 100 American and British copyrighted books is being offered to Japanese publishers for competitive bidding.
subfiles.from: Civil Information and Education Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Announces commercial arrangements offering 100 American and British books for competitive translation bidding by Japanese publishers, providing the full title list.
subfiles.title: SCAP Announces Initial List of 100 Foreign Copyrighted Books Now Available for Publication in Japan (Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 432)

subfiles.about: CIE announces the results of competitive bidding for foreign book translation rights, listing 53 Japanese publishers awarded rights for 91 titles.
subfiles.from: Civil Information and Education Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: CIE announces that 53 Japanese publishers have been awarded translation rights for 91 American and British books, with planned publication of over 2.2 million copies. Average royalties offered were 15 percent, with Joseph C. Grew's 'Ten Years in Japan' receiving the highest bid and George Orwell's 'Animal Farm' attracting the most bids. A comprehensive schedule details each awarded book, winning publisher, royalty rate, advance payment, and proposed print run.
subfiles.title: Fifty-Three Japanese Publishers Awarded Book Translation Rights (Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 432)

subfiles.about: SCAP grants Earnest Hoberecht a license to contract with Radio Shimbun Sha to publish a Japanese edition of 'Democratic Etiquette'.

subfiles.summary: Licenses Earnest Hoberecht to publish a Japanese edition of 'Democratic Etiquette' through Radio Shimbun Sha under occupation financial regulations.
